messages.subject: Estimating the average marginal effect
parts:
I have a hierarchical space-time model investigating the interaction between county-level prescription opioid supply and socioeconomic conditions on drug overdose deaths. Reviewers would like to see the interaction results presented on the additive scale, which is the preferred way to present interaction results in epidemiology. 

Typically, I would do this by switching from the OR or RR to the average marginal effects by transforming back to the probability scale (rather than the log odds, for example) and aggregating (i.e., marginalizing) the effect estimates on the probability scale. However, I have no idea how to do this from a complicated space-time model estimated in R-INLA. 

For this analysis, I fit a hierarchical model with Poisson distribution, using conditional autoregressive random effects to adjust for spatial autocorrelation, a vector of time-varying covariates, state fixed effects, and county random slopes, estimating the interaction using a two-way cross product term. 

Since I'm using restricted data for this analysis, I can't provide data, but I provide the code below (and if needed, I could simulate some data).

#Make a copy of county number for county-level trend 
mydata14$ID <- cumsum(!duplicated(mydata14$COUNTY))
countyTrend <- mydata14$ID
y14 <- mydata14$drug_death
e14 <- as.numeric(mydata14$POP) * sum(y14)/sum(as.numeric(mydata14$POP))

#Create two-way cross-product term
mydata14$PO_supply_X_Unemp <- mydata14$s.PO.supply * mydata14$s.UNEMPRATE

formula.nbin <- y14 ~ 1 + f(ID, model = "bym", graph = Cnty3109.adj, constr = TRUE, scale.model = TRUE) +
                            f(countyTrend, YearNum, model = "iid", constr = TRUE) + 
                            factor(mydata14$STATE) +
                            factor(mydata14$YearNum) + 
                            factor(mydata14$RUCC) + 
                            s.pct.0_19 + 
                            s.pct.20_44 + 
                            s.pct.45_64 +
                            s.pct.male + 
                            s.pct.nhwhite + 
                            s.pct.nhblack +
                            s.pct.hispanic +  
                            s.pct.hs_less +
                            s.pct.collegeplus +
                            s.SPOPDENS +  
                            proportion_of_year_mml_effect +  
                            must_access +
                            s.UNEMPRATE +
                            s.PO.supply +
                            PO_supply_X_Unemp

mod.p <- inla(formula.nbin, family = c("poisson"),
                    data=mydata14, E=e14,
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE),
                    control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE)  )


How could I use the output from this model to estimate the average marginal effects at different levels of the two interaction variables, e.g., the risk of death at -2SD to +2SD of one variable and at the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile of the other variable?
